Q: DTO Explanation A:

You have to be very careful if you use AutoMapper. For example you must know how to use LINQ with AutoMapper. When it is a basic, non-performance related app, I recommend using AutoMapper due to simplicity. On the other hand, AutoMapper might have some serious performance issues in the wrong hands. :)

Q: Why does is.na(NULL) returns logical(0) and not FALSE? A:

If you want is.na(NULL) to return FALSE try testing its return value with isTRUE.

isTRUE(is.na(NULL))
#> [1] FALSE

Created on 2026-01-17 with reprex v2.1.1

From the documentation help("isTRUE"):

isTRUE(x) is the same as { is.logical(x) && length(x) == 1 && !is.na(x) && x }; isFALSE() is defined analogously. Consequently, if(isTRUE(cond)) may be preferable to if(cond) because of NAs.
In earlier R versions, isTRUE <- function(x) identical(x, TRUE), had the drawback to be false e.g., for x <- c(val = TRUE).

Q: eval(substitute()) within a R6 object A:

You can set the parent environment.

A <- R6::R6Class('A', public=list(f1 = 1))
test <- A$new()

eval(substitute(f1 == 1),test)
# Error in f1 == 1 : could not find function "=="
parent.env(test)
# <environment: R_EmptyEnv>
parent.env(test) <- baseenv()
eval(substitute(f1 == 1),test)
# [1] TRUE

This is useful/necessary because for the most part all functions/operators in R are functions or primitives, and they are all found in the search path of namespaces and environments. Since parent.env(test) is originally an "empty env", it will not find any function or primitive.
